slos.description:
define ‘chemistry’ and its various branches:
a. analytical chemistry,
b. astrochemistry,
c. biochemistry,
d. environmental chemistry,
e. geochemistry,
f. industrial chemistry,
g. inorganic chemistry,
h. nuclear chemistry,
i. organic chemistry,
j. physical chemistry,
k. polymer chemistry;
explain the significance of the branches of chemistry mentioned in SLO 1.1.1;
describe the contribution of Jabir Ibn Hayyan and Al-Razi in chemistry during the Islamic Golden Age (8th to 14th centuries);
define the term ‘scientific paradigm’;

subtopics.name: 1.3 Basic Definitions, Comparisons, Valencies, and Chemical Formulae

slos.description:
define the following terms:
a. atoms,
b. elements,
c. compounds,
d. mixtures,
e. molecules;

differentiate between:
a. atoms and molecules,
b. atoms and ions,
c. molecules and molecular ions,
d. ions and free radicals;
differentiate among elements, compounds and mixtures;
classify the chemical species into elements, mixtures, compounds, ions, molecular ions and free radicals;
define the term ‘valency’;
determine valencies of common elements and ions (radicals) independently or in compounds;
determine the formula of a compound based on the valencies of elements and ions (radicals).

examSpec.erqGroup: Combined with Topic 5: 6 Marks (Choose any ONE from TWO)

slos.description:
define the following terms:
a. gram atomic mass,
b. gram molecular mass,
c. gram formula mass,
d. formula unit,
e. mole,
f. Avogadro’s number;
relate gram atomic mass, gram molecular mass and gram formula mass to mole and Avogadro’s number;

calculate the following quantities of chemical species:
a. number of moles,
b. number of particles (atoms, molecules and ions),
c. molar mass (atomic/ molecular/ formula),
d. mass;
differentiate between empirical formula and molecular formula;
calculate the percentage composition by mass of an element in a compound;
calculate the empirical formula using percentages or masses of elements;
calculate the molecular formula using molecular mass and empirical formula;

illustrate the following types of chemical reactions:
a. displacement (single/ double),
b. decomposition,
c. addition/ synthesis/ combination,
d. combustion (complete/ incomplete),
e. neutralisation,
f. hydrolysis;

evaluate the effectiveness of chemical reactions based on the following characteristics:
a. change of state,
b. change in colour,
c. evolution of gas,
d. change in temperature,
e. formation of a precipitate,
f. occurrence of sound;
construct chemical equations and ionic equations to show reactants forming products, including state symbols;
balance chemical equations by inspection or trial and error method;

solve problems based on stoichiometric relationships of substances in terms of:
a. mass,
b. number of moles,
c. number of molecules,
d. mole ratio,
e. volume of gases at Room Temperature and Pressure (RTP) (24 L or dm³ and 24000 mL or cm³).
describe the structure of an atom with reference to the location, relative electric charges and relative masses of proton, electron and neutron;

define the following terms:
a. atomic (proton) number,
b. mass (nucleon) number,
c. atomic mass,
d. atomic mass unit;
calculate the atomic number, mass number, number of electrons and neutrons of atoms and ions;

define the following terms:

b. average atomic mass,
c. relative atomic mass based on C-12 scale,
d. radioactive isotopes,
e. radioactivity;
determine the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in different isotopes of H, C, O, Cl and U;
calculate the relative atomic masses of chlorine and boron by using the mass number and natural abundance of their isotopes;
explain the role of isotopes in carbon dating (carbon), power generation (uranium) and medical imaging (iodine, sodium, technetium, thallium, arsenic, cobalt and xenon);

subtopics.name: 3.3 Models to Understand the Structure of an Atom

slos.description: explain Rutherford’s experiment leading to the discovery of the atomic nucleus;
explain the defects of Rutherford’s atomic model;
describe the main points (postulates) of Bohr’s atomic model;
differentiate between shells and sub-shells of an atom;
deduce the electronic arrangement (in shells) and electronic configuration (of sub-shells) of the first twenty elements and their ions using their atomic number and charges (if any).
state the modern periodic law;
differentiate between a period and a group in the periodic table;
determine the group, period and block of an element using its electronic configuration (first twenty elements);
describe the demarcation of the periodic table into s, p, d, and f-blocks;
determine the location of families on the periodic table based on their characteristics and electronic configuration (representative elements);

define the following terms:
a. shielding effect,
b. electronegativity,
c. atomic radii,
d. electron affinity,
e. ionisation energy (1st and 2nd);

explain the periodic trend of the following within a group and a period of the periodic table:

b. electronegativity,
c. atomic radii,
d. electron affinity,
e. ionisation energy (1st and 2nd);

compare the chemical reactivity and physical properties (metallic character, physical states, conductivity, density, melting and boiling points) of elements in the same family of elements (representative elements);

subtopics.name: 4.3 Properties of Elements in a Group

slos.description: determine elements as an alkali metal, an alkaline earth metal, a halogen and a noble gas based on their electronic configuration;

compare the general properties of metals and non-metals in terms of:

b. density,

g. sonority,

a. existence as monoatomic gases or free state in nature,

a. relative hardness,
b. density,
c. melting and boiling points,
d. variable oxidation states,
e. formation of coloured compounds;

explain the formation of an ionic bond;
explain the general characteristics of ionic compounds;
identify a compound as having ionic bond;
draw electron dot and cross structure of a binary ionic compound, for example, NaCl, MgO, K₂O and CaCl₂;

explain the general characteristics of covalent compounds;

subtopics.name: 6.1 Kinetic Molecular Theory and Phase Changes

slos.description: compare the physical states of matter based on the intermolecular forces present between their molecules;

explain phase changes (melting, freezing, vaporisation, condensation, sublimation and deposition) due to changes in temperature and pressure affecting the arrangement and motion of particles within a substance;

b. effusion,
c. density,
d. compressibility;

d. density,

explain the following physical properties of solids:
a. melting point,
b. density,
c. compressibility;

explain the common rules used for assigning oxidation numbers to free elements, ions, molecules and atoms;
calculate the oxidation number of an atom in a compound and polyatomic ion;

practicals.title: Experiment 1 — Separate a Mixture of Iron Filings, Sand and Alum
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: China dish, funnel, magnet, watch glass, filter paper, funnel stand, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp, glass rod, beaker, match box, tripod stand · Chemicals: Fe (iron filings), alum, sand and water
practicals.description: Employ appropriate physical methods (magnetic separation, dissolution, filtration, and evaporation/crystallisation) to separate a mixture of iron filings, sand and alum.

practicals.title: Experiment 2 — Demonstrate Decomposition Reaction of Calcium Carbonate
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, mortar pestle, safety goggles, match box, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp, test tube holder, one holed stopper with glass tube and rubber tubing or bent tube · Chemicals: Calcium carbonate and lime water (solution of calcium hydroxide)
practicals.description: Demonstrate that compounds can be the products of a decomposition reaction by heating calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) and passing the evolved CO₂ gas through freshly prepared lime water.

practicals.title: Experiment 3 — Measure the Boiling Point of Ethyl Alcohol
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Beaker, iron stand, clamp, glass rod, thermometer, fusion tube, tripod stand, capillary tube, wire gauze, matchbox, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp · Chemicals: Sample of ethyl alcohol and water
practicals.description: Measure the boiling point of ethyl alcohol using a water bath and capillary/fusion tube assembly.

practicals.title: Experiment 4 — Measure the Melting Point of Wax
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Beaker, iron stand, clamp, glass rod, thermometer, capillary tube, tripod stand, wire gauze, match box, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp, thread · Chemicals: Sample of wax and water
practicals.description: Measure the melting point of wax using the capillary tube method in a heated water bath.

practicals.title: Experiment 5 — Demonstrate Sublimation Using Solid Ammonium Chloride
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Test tube, cotton, test tube holder, match box, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp · Chemicals: Ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl)
practicals.description: Demonstrate sublimation using solid ammonium chloride in a cotton-plugged test tube.

practicals.title: Experiment 6 — Prepare 250 cm³ / 1 Litre of 0.1 M Oxalic Acid Solution
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Beaker, glass rod, spatula, balance (physical/digital), funnel, pipette, filter paper/watch glass (for weighing), weight box, volumetric flask (250 cm³ / 1 litre) · Chemicals: Oxalic acid, distilled water
practicals.description: Prepare a standard 250 cm³ (or 1 litre) solution of 0.1 M oxalic acid by accurate weighing and dilution to the calibration mark.

practicals.title: Experiment 7 — Prepare 100 cm³ of 0.01 M Na₂CO₃ Solution from 0.1 M Solution
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Beaker, volumetric flask, stirrer, graduated cylinder or pipette · Chemicals: Distilled water, 0.1 M Na₂CO₃ solution
practicals.description: Prepare 100 cm³ of 0.01 M Na₂CO₃ solution by quantitative dilution (M₁V₁ = M₂V₂) from the given 0.1 M Na₂CO₃ stock solution.

practicals.title: Experiment 8 — Demonstrate That Temperature Affects Solubility
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Beaker, glass rod, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp, tripod stand, wire gauze, match box · Chemicals: Sucrose and water
practicals.description: Demonstrate the effect of temperature on the solubility of sucrose in water.

practicals.title: Experiment 9 — Prepare Crystals of Copper Sulphate
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Beaker, tripod stand, wire gauze, filter paper, china dish, funnel, filter stand, stirrer, match box, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp · Chemicals: Impure copper sulphate and distilled water
practicals.description: Prepare pure crystals of copper(II) sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO₄·5H₂O) from an impure sample via dissolution, filtration, concentration, and crystallisation.

practicals.title: Experiment 10 — Perform Paper Chromatography to Separate an Ink Mixture
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Whatman filter paper No. 1, glass cylinder with a glass support, rubber bung, capillary tubes, lead pencil · Chemicals: Developing solvents (water–alcohol mixture / n-butanol, ethanol and ammonia) and mixture of inks (blue, green, red)
practicals.description: Perform ascending paper chromatography to separate the components of the given ink mixture and determine their retention factors (R_f).

practicals.title: Experiment 11 — Demonstrate the Conductivity of Different Solutions
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Beakers, wires, battery, electrodes, bulb, crocodile clips, bulb holder, stirrer · Chemicals: Distilled water, sugar, NaCl, vinegar, HCl, NaOH and CuSO₄ solution
practicals.description: Demonstrate the electrical conductivity of strong electrolytes, weak electrolytes, and non-electrolytes using an electrode-bulb circuit.

practicals.title: Experiment 12 — Demonstrate Electroplating of Copper Metal on an Iron Strip
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Iron and copper strips, beaker, battery, wires, bulb, bulb holder, crocodile clips · Chemicals: Copper sulphate (CuSO₄) solution
practicals.description: Demonstrate the electrolytic deposition (electroplating) of copper metal onto an iron strip using a copper anode and aqueous copper(II) sulphate electrolyte.

explain the use of chlorine in maintaining the cleanliness of swimming pool;

discuss the causes, symptoms and preventive measures of various types of water-borne diseases, i.e., diarrhoea, cholera, dysentery, cryptosporidiosis, fluorosis, jaundice, hepatitis, typhoid and hookworm infection.

practicals.title: Experiment 1 — Effect of Heat (Temperature) on a Chemical Equilibrium System
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Bunsen burner or hot plate, test tubes, test tube holder, test tube rack, thermometer, goggles · Chemicals: Copper(II) sulphate pentahydrate or cobalt(II) chloride hexahydrate and distilled water
practicals.description: Demonstrate the reversible effect of heat (temperature) on a chemical equilibrium system using hydrated copper(II) sulphate (CuSO₄·5H₂O) or cobalt(II) chloride hexahydrate (CoCl₂·6H₂O).

practicals.title: Experiment 2 — Measure the pH of Different Solutions Using pH Paper
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Beakers, pH paper, pH scale, watch glass, stirrer · Chemicals: Baking soda, HCl, soap solution, curd, garden soil, table salt, caustic soda, vinegar, lemon juice, apple juice, orange juice and oxalic acid
practicals.description: Measure the pH of household and laboratory solutions using universal indicator pH paper and classify them as acidic, neutral, or basic.

practicals.title: Experiment 3 — Standardise the Given Solution of Sodium Hydroxide Volumetrically
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Burette, iron stand, funnel, clamp, pipette, beakers, conical flasks, dropper · Chemicals: Sodium hydroxide solution, standard solution of hydrochloric acid, phenolphthalein
practicals.description: Standardise the given sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution volumetrically by acid-base titration against a standard hydrochloric acid (HCl) solution using phenolphthalein indicator.

practicals.title: Experiment 4 — Measure the Exact Molarity of a Solution of Oxalic Acid Volumetrically
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Burette, iron stand, funnel, clamp, pipette, beakers, conical flasks, dropper · Chemicals: Standard solution of NaOH, oxalic acid solution, phenolphthalein
practicals.description: Determine the exact molarity of a given oxalic acid ((COOH)₂·2H₂O) solution volumetrically by titrating against a standard sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution.

practicals.title: Experiment 5 — Silver Nitrate Test to Detect Chloride (Cl⁻), Bromide (Br⁻), and Iodide (I⁻) Ions
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Test-tube, test-tube stand, stirrer · Chemicals: NaI, NaBr, NaCl, AgNO₃, and NH₄OH
practicals.description: Perform the silver nitrate (AgNO₃) precipitation and ammonium hydroxide (NH₄OH) solubility test to detect and distinguish chloride (Cl⁻), bromide (Br⁻), and iodide (I⁻) halide ions.

practicals.title: Experiment 6 — Flame Test to Detect Calcium, Strontium, Barium, and Copper Ions
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Platinum wire / glass rod, match box, watch glass, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp · Chemicals: Salt of each ion: calcium (Ca²⁺), strontium (Sr²⁺), barium (Ba²⁺), and copper (Cu²⁺) and concentrated HCl
practicals.description: Perform a flame test to detect the presence of calcium (brick-red), strontium (crimson-red), barium (apple-green), and copper (bluish-green) ions by observing their characteristic flame colours.

practicals.title: Experiment 7 — Sodium Nitroprusside Test to Detect Ketones
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp, match box, dropper, water bath · Chemicals: Fructose solution, distilled water, sodium nitroprusside solid and sodium hydroxide solution
practicals.description: Perform the alkaline sodium nitroprusside test to detect the presence of a ketone functional group (formation of a wine-red colouration).

practicals.title: Experiment 8 — Fehling’s and Tollens’ Tests to Detect Aldehydes
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp, match box, water bath, dropper · Chemicals: Formaldehyde, Tollens’ reagent, Fehling’s solution and glucose solution
practicals.description: Perform Fehling’s test (brick-red Cu₂O precipitate) and Tollens’ silver mirror test to detect the presence of an aldehyde functional group.

practicals.title: Experiment 9 — Sodium Carbonate / Bicarbonate Limewater Test to Detect Carboxylic Acids
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, delivery tube, dropper · Chemicals: Limewater, carboxylic acid, solid sodium carbonate and distilled water
practicals.description: Perform the sodium carbonate test (with limewater confirmation of brisk CO₂ effervescence) to detect the presence of carboxylic acids.

practicals.title: Experiment 10 — Ferric Chloride (FeCl₃) Test to Detect Phenol
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, dropper · Chemicals: Phenol solution, freshly prepared ferric chloride solution and distilled water
practicals.description: Perform the neutral ferric chloride (FeCl₃) test to detect the presence of phenol (formation of a violet/purple complex).

practicals.title: Experiment 11 — Potassium Permanganate (KMnO₄) Baeyer’s Test for Unsaturation
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Test tubes, test tube holder, test tube stand, dropper · Chemicals: Cinnamic acid solution, ghee, vegetable oil and KMnO₄ solution
practicals.description: Perform the alkaline potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) test to differentiate between saturated and unsaturated organic compounds by observing decolourisation of purple KMnO₄.

practicals.title: Experiment 12 — Demonstrate Softening of Permanent and Temporary Hard Water
practicals.apparatus: Equipment: Beaker, test tubes, china dish, funnel, iron stand, filter paper, Bunsen burner or spirit lamp · Chemicals: Water sample (beakers containing two types of hard water), lime water, small soap bar, sodium carbonate solution and sodium zeolite
practicals.description: Demonstrate the softening of temporary hard water (by boiling / Clark’s limewater method) and permanent hard water (by adding washing soda Na₂CO₃ or passing through sodium zeolite).
